topic.title: What lies under Grand Central Terminal: the shuttle, the 4/5/6, the 7, the secret M42 power basement and Grand Central Madison's deep platforms

title: How Deep Does Grand Central Go?
description:
How deep does Grand Central go?
Below New York's most famous station run the shuttle, two more subway lines, a secret power basement and the deep platforms of Grand Central Madison.
Sources: Wikipedia, ASCE, MTA (2026).
Depths from published sources. Cutaway illustrations, not to scale.
cta: Which station should we dive under next? Comment

lines.text: Grand Central has trains stacked under trains. How deep does it go?
20 ft: the shuttle to Times Square.
50 ft: the four, five and six trains.
80 ft: the seven train to Queens. And below that?
105 ft: M Forty-Two, a secret basement full of power machines.
150 ft: Grand Central Madison, the deepest platforms.
The escalator ride up takes 90 s.
Just to get back up to Grand Central.

notes: 6 figures computed from inputs; 6 cross-checked against closed-form formulas.

note: 1 beats between the hook and the payoff open a new question; at least 2 ("But that's not where the dealer makes his money.", "So why would he give it away?"): the viewer always waits for something

All 6 facts confirmed on their source pages (WebFetch 2026-11-21): Wikipedia Grand Central-42nd St 'Relative depths' lists Shuttle 20 ft, Lexington 50 ft, Flushing 80 ft, LIRR lower level 150 ft; Wikipedia M42 '105 to 109 feet'; ASCE 'roughly 150 ft below street level'; MTA guide '182-feet... one-way trip takes about 90-seconds'. Verify list: Madison 150 ft agreed by ASCE and Wikipedia; M42 shown at the low end of 105-109 ft. Story current (Madison opened 2023). Shuttle to Times Square, 7 to Queens, Madison deepest platforms, M42 a power substation left off maps: all match sources; no security details beyond published. Description ends with the channel disclaimer. Notes (not blocking): MTA says 'about 90 seconds' for the escalators (script says 'takes 90 s'), and the ride ends at the Madison concourse inside Grand Central, not street level; M42 depth is 'thought to be' 105-109 ft.
